questions.question: In the course's diet problem, pigs are fed a mix of two feeds, A and B. What do the decision variables $x_A$ and $x_B$ represent?
options: The prices per pound of feed A and of feed B
The pounds of feed A and of feed B in the daily mix
The calories and vitamins supplied by the daily mix
The minimum daily requirements for the two nutrients

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. What does its objective express?
options: Minimize the daily cost of the feed mix
Maximize the calories in the daily feed mix
Minimize the total weight of the feed
Maximize the share of the cheaper feed

questions.question: In the diet LP, the nutrient constraints $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ and $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ use $\ge$. Why that direction?
options: They are upper limits that the mix must never go above.
They are minimum requirements the mix must meet or beat.
They must hold with equality for every feasible mix.
The direction is free, since the cost is being minimized.

questions.question: In the diet LP, $x_A$ and $x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B. What does the constraint $2x_A-x_B\le0$ require?
options: Feed A makes up at least one-third of the total weight.
Feed B makes up at most one-third of the total weight.
Feed A makes up at most one-half of the total weight.
Feed A makes up at most one-third of the total weight.

questions.question: The diet LP is solved graphically by drawing lines of equal cost. How is the cheapest feasible mix found?
options: Slide the cost line away from the origin until it last touches the region.
Take the feasible point of the region that is closest to the origin.
Take the point where the calorie and vitamin lines intersect.
Slide the cost line toward lower cost until it first touches the region.

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. Which daily mix is feasible?
The optimal daily mix of the diet LP uses $x_A=\frac{20}{7}$ pounds of feed A and $x_B=\frac{40}{7}$ pounds of feed B, with prices 0.4 and 0.8 per pound. What is its daily cost?
With $x_A$ and $x_B$ the pounds of feeds A and B, which linear constraint says that feed A is at most one-third of the total feed weight?
options: $x_A-3x_B\le0$
$3x_A-x_B\le0$
$x_A-2x_B\le0$
$2x_A-x_B\le0$

questions.question: A simplified diet model minimizes $2x_A+3x_B$ subject to $x_A+2x_B\ge6$, $3x_A+x_B\ge6$ and $x_A,x_B\ge0$. What is its optimal mix?
options: $(0,6)$, with cost 18
$(6,0)$, with cost 12

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. At the optimum $x_A=\frac{20}{7}$, $x_B=\frac{40}{7}$, which constraints hold with equality?
options: Calories and vitamins, not the share
Calories and the share of feed A
Vitamins and the share of feed A
All three constraints at once

questions.question: Suppose the two nutrient requirements of the diet LP were mistakenly written with $\le$ instead of $\ge$, with everything else unchanged. What would minimizing cost then recommend?
options: The same mix as before
Buying no feed, at cost 0
Only feed B, the costlier one
No mix, the model is infeasible

questions.question: The feasible region of the diet LP is unbounded. Why does the LP still have a finite optimal cost?
options: The feasible region is in fact bounded by the share constraint.
The cost is maximized, so an unbounded region causes no problem.
The share constraint caps the amount of feed B in the mix.
The cost is at least 0, as amounts and prices are nonnegative.

questions.question: In the diet LP, feed A gives 800 calorie units for 0.4 per pound and feed B gives 1000 for 0.8 per pound. Why does the share-of-A constraint hold with equality at the optimum?
options: Feed B is cheaper per calorie, so the mix uses as little A as allowed.
A share constraint always holds with equality at an optimal mix.
Feed B is costlier per calorie, so the mix uses as much A as allowed.
Feed A supplies more calories per pound than feed B does.

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. If the share constraint is dropped, what becomes the optimal mix?
options: $(\frac{5}{3},\frac{20}{3})$, with cost 6
$(10,0)$, with cost 4
$(0,10)$, with cost 8

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. The price of feed A rises from 0.4 to 0.8 per pound, so the objective becomes $0.8x_A+0.8x_B$. What is the new optimum?
options: $(0,10)$, with cost $8$
$(10,0)$, with cost $8$

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. The share rule is relaxed to feed A at most one-half of the total weight, so $2x_A-x_B\le0$ becomes $x_A-x_B\le0$. What is the new optimum?
options: $(10,0)$, with cost $4$
$(5,5)$, with cost $6$

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day. At the optimum the vitamin constraint is not tight (800 versus 700). An analyst concludes that it excludes no mix and can be deleted. Which assessment is correct?
options: Right: a constraint that is not tight at the optimum excludes no feasible mix at all.
Wrong: deleting it changes the optimum, since every constraint must be tight at it.
Wrong: $(0,8)$ meets calories and share but not vitamins; the optimum is unaffected.
Right: the vitamin requirement is implied by the calorie requirement for every mix.

questions.question: With $x_A$ and $x_B$ the pounds of feeds A and B, a student writes the share rule as $x_A\le x_B/3$. What does this constraint actually require?
options: Feed A at most a quarter of the total feed weight
Feed A at most one-third of the total feed weight
Feed B at most one-third of the total feed weight
Feed A at most three times the weight of feed B

questions.question: Consider the diet LP without the share constraint: minimize $0.7x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$, $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ and $x_A,x_B\ge0$. Feed A is cheaper per pound. What does the optimal mix look like?
options: Only feed B, 10 pounds, costing 8
Only feed A, 10 pounds, costing 7
A mix of the two feeds, costing 6.5
Only feed B, 8 pounds, costing 6.4

questions.question: The diet LP is minimize $0.4x_A+0.8x_B$ subject to $800x_A+1000x_B\ge8000$ (calories), $140x_A+70x_B\ge700$ (vitamins), $2x_A-x_B\le0$ (share of feed A) and $x_A,x_B\ge0$, where $x_A,x_B$ are the pounds of feeds A and B per day; its optimum is $(\frac{20}{7},\frac{40}{7})$. The vitamin requirement 700 is replaced by a value $r$. For which $r$ does $(\frac{20}{7},\frac{40}{7})$ remain optimal?
options: Exactly for $r\le800$
Exactly for $r\le700$
Exactly for $700\le r\le800$
For every value of $r$
